name: dpia
description: Draft a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) for one processing activity in the structure GDPR Article 35(7) requires — a systematic description of the processing and its purposes, necessity and proportionality, risks to the rights and freedoms of individuals, and the measures to address them — with a data inventory (categories, special category data, data subjects, sources, recipients, transfers outside the EEA, retention), the lawful basis per purpose, a likelihood × severity risk table scored for harm to people, residual risk, a view on prior consultation, and the open questions for the DPO. Use when the user needs a DPIA or PIA, is launching something that processes personal data in a new or risky way, or asks "do we need a DPIA", "write the DPIA for…", "privacy impact assessment".

handoff.when: the processing runs on a new system whose security design hasn't been assessed
handoff.purpose: Find the security threats to the system so the DPIA's measures section can cite them.
handoff.fallback: If threat-model is absent, list the security measures the vendor or team states (access control, encryption, logging) in §5 and add a DPO question asking for a security review.

handoff.when: the DPIA leaves residual risks the business has accepted
handoff.purpose: Track the accepted residual risks with an owner and review date alongside other organisational risks.
handoff.fallback: If risk-register is absent, list each accepted residual risk with its owner and review trigger in §8.

model.rationale: Legal-structure judgment: screening, choosing a lawful basis per purpose, spotting inferred special category data and transfers, and scoring harm to individuals. Errors are costly and the input is usually incomplete.
